1.title: GitHub Actions Basics
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Git Hub Actions Basics. It covers the exam area Part five: Automation and safety. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Explain event, workflow, job, step, action and runner. Write a first workflow that runs on push and by hand. Filter triggers by branch, path and schedule. Read a run and its logs. Use contexts, env, vars and secrets in expressions and if conditions. Run jobs in parallel or in order with needs. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Course
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the course. Part: Part five: Automation and safety. Verified with: the Git Hub documentation (read twenty twenty-six-eleven to sixteen); workflow files checked for syntax, not run.

1.title: What Was Executed and What Is Reference Only
1.text: What Was Executed and What Is Reference Only. Workflow files run on Git Hub and were not run there. They were checked for syntax and against Git Hub's workflow schema, and the shell commands in them were run locally.

1.title: The Actions model
1.text: The Actions model. Git Hub Actions is the automation built into Git Hub. Something happens in the repository, Git Hub starts a workflow, and a fresh machine runs its steps. The figure shows how the parts nest.

1.title: The Actions model, continued
1.text: The Actions model. The figure shows this: An event starts a workflow, the workflow holds jobs, and each job runs its steps on its own runner.

1.title: The Actions model, continued
1.text: The Actions model. Event. Something that starts a workflow: a push, a pull request, a schedule, a click. Workflow. One yammel file: which events start it and which jobs it runs. Job. A set of steps on one runner; jobs run in parallel unless one needs another. Step. One shell command ( run ) or one action ( uses ); steps run in order. Action. A reusable unit of work, for example actions slash checkout. Runner. The server that runs one job; every job gets a fresh virtual machine.

1.title: The Actions model, continued
1.text: The Actions model. Workflows live in the folder dot github slash workflows as dot yml or dot yaml files. They are ordinary files: versioned, reviewed in pull requests and tied to a branch. A workflow runs on an event, on a schedule or by hand. Git Hub-hosted runners have labels such as ubuntu latest (Ubuntu twenty-four point zero four), windows latest and macos latest (on arm sixty-four). The -latest labels point to the newest stable image and can change. Standard runners are free in public repositories; private repositories use the compute included in the plan. Larger and self-hosted runners also exist (module fifteen). Tip: Treat workflow files as code: change them through a branch and a pull request. They sit in the repository like any other file, and a bad edit can break every later run or leak a secret.

1.title: A first workflow and how to read a run
1.text: A first workflow and how to read a run. The smallest useful workflow runs on a push and by hand, prints a message and checks out the code. A runner starts empty, so a job that needs your files must run actions slash checkout first. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: A first workflow and how to read a run, continued
1.text: A first workflow and how to read a run. on. The events that start the workflow: a push to main, or a click on Run workflow. workflow dispatch. Lets someone start the run by hand; the file must be on the default branch for the Run workflow button. runs on. The runner label for the job. uses. Runs an action; actions slash checkout at v six copies the repository onto the runner. run. Runs shell commands; the default shell on Linux and mac O S is bash dash e zero, so a step stops at its first failing command. Try it: save the file, commit it and push. Your hash will differ.

1.title: A first workflow and how to read a run, continued
1.text: A first workflow and how to read a run. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: A first workflow and how to read a run, continued
1.text: A first workflow and how to read a run. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: A first workflow and how to read a run, continued
1.text: A first workflow and how to read a run. After the push the run starts by itself. Open the Actions tab, choose the run, then choose a job to see its steps. Every step has its own log. A failed step turns the job red, and the later steps are skipped unless their if says otherwise. A run on a pull request also shows in the Checks tab of that P R. Tip: Start every job that needs your code with actions slash checkout. Each job gets a fresh runner, and a fresh runner has no copy of the repository.

1.title: Triggers and filters
1.text: Triggers and filters. The on key chooses the events. Filters narrow an event so the workflow does not run for every change. push. Starts when: Commits are pushed. Details: Filters: branches, branches ignore, tags, tags ignore, paths, paths ignore. pull request. Starts when: A P R is opened, gets new commits or is reopened. Details: These are the default types; no run while the P R has a merge conflict. workflow dispatch. Starts when: Someone clicks Run workflow. Details: inputs of type string, number, boolean, choice or environment. schedule. Starts when: A cron time arrives. Details: pozix cron in U T C, never more often than every five minutes; runs on the default branch.

1.title: Triggers and filters, continued
1.text: Triggers and filters. A cron line has five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. In a public repository a scheduled workflow is disabled automatically after sixty days without activity. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Triggers and filters, continued
1.text: Triggers and filters. This file starts on a push to main that changes a file under src, on every pull request, every Monday at five:thirty U T C and on a click that offers staging or production. Tip: If a required check comes from a workflow with a path filter, remember that a skipped workflow leaves the check Pending. The pull request then waits for a result that never comes.

1.title: Contexts, variables and conditions
1.text: Contexts, variables and conditions. The text... is an expression. Git Hub replaces it with its value before the step runs. The values come from contexts. github. Example: github dot ref. What it holds: Facts about the run, such as the branch or tag ( refs slash heads slash main ) and github dot event name. env. Example: env dot app. What it holds: Variables set with env; a step beats a job, and a job beats the workflow.

2.title: Contexts, variables and conditions, continued
2.text: Contexts, variables and conditions. vars. Example: vars dot region. What it holds: Plain, non-secret variables saved in the repository settings. secrets. Example: secrets dot token. What it holds: Secret values saved in Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions; an unset secret is an empty string.

2.title: Contexts, variables and conditions, continued
2.text: Contexts, variables and conditions. An if: condition decides whether a job or step runs. Write it without the braces: if github dot ref refs slash heads slash main. After a failure, if always still runs a step and if failure runs it only when an earlier step failed. A secret cannot be used directly in an if; module fourteen shows the way around it. Tip: Hand values to a step through env and read them as shell variables. The script then holds a plain R E F instead of text pasted in by Git Hub, which is safer for values that people can write (module fifteen).

2.title: Jobs in parallel, in order, and as checks
2.text: Jobs in parallel, in order, and as checks. Jobs run in parallel by default, each on its own runner. They share nothing unless you upload and download an artifact (module fourteen). The key needs makes a job wait for one or more others, and it does not start if a job it needs failed. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

2.title: Jobs in parallel, in order, and as checks, continued
2.text: Jobs in parallel, in order, and as checks. Here lint and test start together. report waits for both and runs only on the main branch. A workflow with the pull request trigger runs on the pull request. Each of its jobs shows as a check in the Checks tab and in the merge box. An admin can make a check required in a branch protection rule or a ruleset (module eleven), and then the pull request cannot merge until that check is green.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A workflow has on workflow dispatch, but the Run workflow button is missing. The file exists only on a feature branch. What fixes it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Merge the workflow file into the default branch. The Run workflow button needs the workflow file on the default branch.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A workflow uses cron zero six one, and the team works far from the U T C time zone. When does the schedule run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Every Monday at six:zero U T C, whatever the local time zone is. Scheduled workflows use pozix cron in U T C by default.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A run page shows lint green, test red and report skipped. The report job has needs lint, test. Why was it skipped? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A job that it needs failed, so it never started. A job with needs does not start when one of the jobs it needs failed.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A step reads secrets dot A P I K E Y, but nobody has created that secret yet. What does the step get? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An empty string, and the run keeps going. An unset secret is evaluated as an empty string.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A required check comes from a workflow with paths src slash. A pull request changes only readme dot md. What does the pull request show? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The check stays Pending because the filter skipped it. A workflow skipped by a filter leaves its required check Pending.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A job has one step, run ls, and the listing is empty although the repository has files. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The job has no checkout step, so the runner has no code. Each job starts on a fresh runner, so it needs actions slash checkout to get the code.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. In which folder do workflow files live? Answer: dot github slash workflows. Question two. What is the difference between a job and a step? Answer: A job is a set of steps on one runner; a step is one command or one action. Question three. Which event adds a Run workflow button? Answer: workflow dispatch.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which time zone does a schedule cron use? Answer: U T C. Question five. Which key makes one job wait for another? Answer: needs. Question six. Which context holds the plain variables saved in the repository settings? Answer: vars.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Model: event starts a workflow; a workflow has jobs. Where: dot github slash workflows, dot yml or dot yaml, reviewed like code. First workflow: on push and workflow dispatch; runs on; actions slash checkout; run. Triggers: push and pull request with filters; schedule in U T C. Contexts: github, env, vars, secrets inside; hand values over with env. Conditions: if without braces; always and failure; no secrets directly. Jobs: parallel by default; needs makes order; a failed need skips the job. Checks: pull request jobs become checks; a skipped filter leaves a required check Pending.
